newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Fischer calls for GST trade-off.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Fischer calls for GST trade-off.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Tuesday the government should abolish the fuel excise if it introduced a goods and service tax (GST).

"If we are going to have a consumption tax, I want movement on fuel excise," Fischer told a National Farmers' Federation conference. "It would be absolutely unacceptable to put a consumption tax -- at whatever rate -- on top of fuel excise."
Fischer recommended that the farmers call for a 100 percent reduction as part of the tax reform debate.

"If you ask me how much reduction I would like to see in fuel excise, then I have no hesitation in saying that a 100 percent in fuel excise -- in other words, no fuel excise -- would suit me just fine," he said. All fuel has been subject to an excise duty for many years, imposed with the original intention of being used for road maintenance and construction.
Farmers and miners get a rebate for diesel used for off-road purposes but they have long argued that the tax harms exports because it makes the cost of transporting their goods so expensive.
The possible introduction of a GST has again become an issue after Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday that the government would have to look at reforming the tax system at some stage.

The conservative Liberal-National government promised before the March 1996 election not to introduce a GST, but has since qualified that promise by saying it would not introduce such a tax in its first term.
The coalition was widely perceived to have lost the 1993 election as a result of plans to introduce a GST.
